text:
We often treat personal knowledge management like a machine, relying on automated captures and AI-driven connections to organize our thoughts. But there is a limit to what an algorithm can synthesize.

A manual fallback—the act of slowing down to hand-write a note or re-type a summary—is essential when you need to move from mere collection to true comprehension. Automation is great for storage, but manual intervention is what turns raw data into integrated wisdom.
